title: Platform systems & services — team wiki, playbook, runbooks, dashboards and roadmap (2026 Q1)
author: Ava Chen
content:
Summary
-------
This consolidated team wiki and playbook summarizes the Platform (systems & services) operational model, runbooks, dashboard/alert standards, quarterly roadmap priorities, and maintenance procedures. It is designed for on-call engineers, service owners, and new platform hires to find consistent guidance for service lifecycle, incident response, and observability.

Scope
-----
Covers the core platform systems and services we operate: control plane services (api-gateway, auth, config-store), runtime fleet (inference-proxy, model-runtime, cache-coordinator), infra services (k8s control, node-provisioner, storage), and platform tooling (ci-cd, infra-as-code, monitoring). Not included: product-facing application logic owned by product teams.

Owner and contacts
------------------
- Primary owner: Platform Engineering (team lead: Marcos Silva)
- On-call rotation: eng-platform oncall (pager: #eng-platform-oncall)
- Escalation: Head of SRE (Diego Martinez) -> VP Engineering (Priya Nair)

Systems & services inventory (high level)
----------------------------------------
| Service name       | Purpose                                 | Primary owner      | SLO (p95)     | Criticality |
|--------------------|-----------------------------------------|--------------------|---------------|-------------|
| api-gateway        | Public REST/SDK ingress, auth, routing  | platform-api team  | 99.95%        | P0          |
| inference-proxy    | Request routing to backend runtimes     | runtime team       | 99.9%         | P0          |
| model-runtime      | GPU-backed inference processes          | runtime team       | 99.9%         | P0          |
| cache-coordinator  | Prefix/KV cache for low-latency reuse   | platform-cache     | 99.8%         | P1          |
| config-store       | Central config and rollout control      | platform-config    | 99.95%        | P1          |
| node-provisioner   | Autoscaling & node lifecycle manager    | infra-provisioning | 99.5%         | P1          |

Note: SLOs above are team-level targets. See per-service SLO documents (links in related_pages).

How-tos (common procedures)
---------------------------
1) Onboard a new service to platform observability
   - Checklist:
     a) Add Prometheus metrics group: service_name_* (latency, errors, succeeded_requests, queue_depth)
     b) Expose OpenTelemetry traces with service and span names (use platform-trace semantic conventions)
     c) Add Grafana dashboard using the template: grafana/platform-service-template.json
     d) Add alert rules in prometheus/rules/service_name.rules.yml (see example below)
     e) Add SLO + burn rate to the SLO registry (slo-registry/services.csv)

   - CLI example:
     ```bash
     # scaffold dashboard and alerts
     tools/platform-scaffold create-service --name my-service 
         --metrics "my_service_" --team "runtime"
     ```

2) Adding a dashboard (recommended minimal panels)
   - Panels to include: 1) latency p50/p95/p99, 2) 5xx error rate, 3) request throughput, 4) queue/deque length, 5) CPU/GPU utilization, 6) heap/memory RSS, 7) 1m/5m pod restart count.
   - Tag dashboard with team and criticality: tags: [platform, runtime, p0]

3) Alert rule example (Prometheus)
   - File: prometheus/rules/inference-proxy.rules.yml
   - Example rule (text):
     ALERT High5xxRate
     IF sum(rate(http_server_errors_total{job="inference-proxy"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="inference-proxy"}[5m])) > 0.01
     FOR 5m
     LABELS { severity="page" }
     ANNOTATIONS { summary="inference-proxy: >1% 5xx errors (5m)" }

Dashboards and alerts standards
------------------------------
- Dashboards must be saved in JSON and checked into the repo: infra/observability/dashboards/<service>.json
- All P0 services require a single-pane overview dashboard (SLO, error rate, latency timers) and an incident triage dashboard (resource metrics, pod details).
- Alert severity mapping:
  - page: immediate pager duty (P0/P1 incidents)
  - ticket: create JIRA to track degradation (P2)
  - silent: metric for visibility only
- Default alert thresholds (tune per-service):
  - p95 latency spike: >2x nominal for 10m -> ticket
  - 5xx error rate: >1% sustained for 5m -> page
  - CPU/GPU saturation: >90% for 5m -> ticket
  - Pod restarts: >5 in 10m -> page

Runbooks (select playbooks)
--------------------------
1) Incident: inference-proxy high latency (pager)
   1. Acknowledge the pager.
   2. Open the incident channel: #inc-inference-proxy-<INCIDENT_ID>.
   3. Check labeled dashboards: Service Overview -> Latency spikes (p95/p99), queue_depth, pod_cpu.
   4. Run quick checks:
      - kubectl get pods -n inference -l app=inference-proxy
      - kubectl top pods -n inference
      - curl -sS http://inference-proxy/health || true
   5. Determine root cause indicants:
      - Queue growth + CPU/GPU low -> worker starvation/config change
      - Pod OOMs -> memory leak; check recent deployments
      - Backend model-runtime errors -> fallbacks triggered (check logs)
   6. Mitigation steps (in order):
      a) Scale inference-proxy replicas (kubectl scale deployment inference-proxy --replicas=<n+2>)
      b) If CPU bound, adjust request/limit or restart unhealthy pods (kubectl rollout restart)
      c) If backend model-runtime is erroring, bypass with fallback route and rollback recent model rollout
      d) Engage runtime team if model artifacts are implicated (tag: @runtime-oncall)
   7. Post-incident: open postmortem template, tag owners, add corrective action to roadmap if needed.

2) Incident: model-runtime node GPU failure (page)
   - Immediate: cordon node (kubectl cordon <node>) and move pods (kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data <node>)
   - Check GPU node health (nvidia-smi), driver logs, and node exporter metrics.
   - If hardware failure suspected, create ticket with infra-provisioning and mark node for replacement.
   - Re-populate capacity using node-provisioner autoscaler profile: set override to +20% for 30m.

Retrospectives and incident reviews
----------------------------------
- Quarterly retro process:
  1) Every quarter, gather incidents with SEV>=P1 and create retro notes in this wiki section.
  2) For each incident include: timeline, detection source, root cause, mitigations, action items, and owners.
  3) Track action items in the platform backlog with milestone tags (Q2-2026).
- Example action items from last retro (Q4-2025):
  - Implement per-model cold-start metric (owner: runtime)
  - Reduce default model-runtime p95 tail by 20% via batching config (owner: runtime-research)

Roadmap (next 3 quarters)
------------------------
- Q1 2026 (current):
  - Complete unified dashboard templates for P0/P1 services (deliverable: grafana templates + onboarding script)
  - Launch automated SLO burn-rate alerts integrated with incident playbooks
  - Improve node-provisioner cold-start from 60s -> 20s for GPU fleets
- Q2 2026:
  - Workload-aware autoscaler for model-runtime based on prefix cache hit rates
  - Per-tenant observability and cost breakdown in Console (beta)
- Q3 2026:
  - Private deployment observability bundle (on-prem Grafana + Prometheus recipes)
  - Enhanced regression alerts tied to eval prompt-sets

Team wiki maintenance & conventions
----------------------------------
- Naming: filenames and page titles use kebab-case with year quarter suffix when applicable (e.g., platform-playbook-runbooks-2026-q1).
- Ownership: each page must list a primary owner and an alternate reviewer. Update the page after any runbook change and bump last_updated.
- Review cadence: core runbooks reviewed every 90 days. Dashboards evaluated after any model or infra rollouts.

Appendix: useful commands & snippets
-----------------------------------
- Get recent errors from logs (kubectl + jq):
  ```bash
  kubectl logs -n inference deployment/inference-proxy --since=15m | jq -R 'fromjson? | select(.level=="error")' | head -n 200
  ```
- Sample Grafana panel JSON path:
  infra/observability/dashboards/inference-proxy-overview.json
- SLO declaration CSV columns: service, slo_name, objective, window_days, owner_email

Related pages
-------------
- Platform operations playbook: /confluence/eng-platform/platform-operations-playbook-2026
- Service-specific runbooks: see infra/runbooks/<service> directory in repo (linked from each service page).

Revision history
----------------
- 2025-11-12: Created (Ava Chen)
- 2026-01-05: Added GPU node failure playbook and autoscaler guidance (Marcos Silva)
- 2026-02-15: Updated alert thresholds and roadmap Q2 items (Priya Nair)

This document is intended to be a living, canonical reference. If you have suggestions or find inaccuracies, please open a PR against infra/docs or ping the owners listed above.
